dedupe_keys.name: fao and ruaf city region food systems programme assessments and resilience planning in pilot city regions 2014 to 2027

description: This case study covers the City Region Food Systems programme, co-run by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the RUAF Global Partnership, which helps national and local governments assess and plan the food systems that link a city with its surrounding rural areas. Phase 1, from 2014 to 2018, worked with Colombo in Sri Lanka, Kitwe and Lusaka in Zambia, Medellín in Colombia, Toronto and the Greater Golden Horseshoe in Canada, Utrecht in the Netherlands and Quito in Ecuador. Phase 2, from 2019 to 2024, focused on resilience to multiple shocks and stresses, including climate and pandemic, in Antananarivo, Colombo, Kigali and Tamale. Phase 3, from 2025 to 2027, works on food loss and waste in Lusaka and Medellín. RUAF led the assessment and planning method, published as the CRFS Handbook with an online toolkit and sustainability and resilience indicator frameworks, and with FAO and CIRAD studied lessons from multiple shocks in a 2024 report. Assessment reports, fact sheets and action plans for the pilot cities are free to read online on the FAO programme website. Coverage is the pilot city regions on four continents. Caveats: outputs are city reports of varying depth, and the programme page summarises results only qualitatively, as stronger local capacity and evidence to identify bottlenecks and vulnerable actors. Simulation uses: city region food flow assessments and resilience indicators for urban food supply planning. Related records: the Baltimore food system resilience planning (case_study-baltimore-food-system-resilience-planning) is a comparable city exercise.
